patch.summary:
Choose Buffer only if your buying job matches “Social media scheduling, analytics, and engagement with a free plan and per-channel Essent” rather than Kartra's shape. Choose Kartra only if your buying job matches “Kartra combines landing pages, email/SMS marketing, memberships/courses, checkouts, funnel” rather than Buffer's shape. Workflow advantage: Buffer leans social-media-marketing, content-marketing; Kartra leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Positioning: Buffer is Social media scheduling, analytics, and engagement with a free plan and per-channel Essentials/Team pricing.; Kartra is Kartra combines landing pages, email/SMS marketing, memberships/courses, checkouts, funnels, AI copy, and related automation in one platform.
- Company-size focus: Buffer (micro, small-business, mid-market) vs Kartra (small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Buffer-leaning social-media-marketing, content-marketing, brand-monitoring vs Kartra-leaning —.
- Researched limits: Buffer — Free plan caps channels and scheduled posts; Kartra — All-in-one breadth can be heavier than a dedicated ESP or scheduler.

Limitations — Buffer: Free plan caps channels and scheduled posts; Not a social listening command center like Brand24; Kartra: All-in-one breadth can be heavier than a dedicated ESP or scheduler; Lower tiers cap contacts, pages, and AI uses.

Poor-fit cases: Buffer is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Free plan caps channels and scheduled posts · Kartra is a poor fit when that limitation bites: All-in-one breadth can be heavier than a dedicated ESP or scheduler · Avoid Buffer if you actually need Kartra's motion (Kartra combines landing pages, email/SMS marketing, memberships/courses, checkou)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
